limitations: Small fixed custom benchmark, not SWE-bench or a general coding ranking.
Nine answer tasks and one real read-tool task; no patches generated or executed.
Independent nonpersistent Pi sessions; extensions and built-in MCP disabled.
Same provider platform, not necessarily the same upstream infrastructure.
Requested high for both; Flint decides when to reason and has no effort control.
Existing Pi settings and project context retained; provider sampling defaults retained.
Wall time includes startup, network, inference and all tool turns.
Token counters and costs are reported by Pi; counters are not cross-tokenizer equivalents.
No automatic retries; unsuccessful responses count as failures.
metadata.grading_note: Read paths are resolved to the target file; equivalent absolute and relative paths are accepted. Original raw results remain unchanged.

results.name: binary_search_repair
results.prompt: A binary search on ascending a uses inclusive bounds lo=0,hi=len(a)-1; while lo < hi: mid=(lo+hi)//2; if a[mid]==x return mid; elif a[mid]<x set lo=mid; else set hi=mid; after loop return -1. Which patch is fully correct, terminating and handles empty/singleton arrays? A: only change loop to lo<=hi. B: loop lo<=hi, set lo=mid+1 and hi=mid-1. C: loop lo<hi, set lo=mid+1 and hi=mid-1. D: only change hi initialization to len(a). Return {"choice":"A/B/C/D"}.
